findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The placeholder convention also scans verbatim claim and card quotes, so a studied system whose source uses UNRESOLVED (or 'not examined') can never pass
findings.evidence: Today the check runs over each file's raw text: rules.rs:1588-1592 checks `text.contains("UNRESOLVED")` and `text.to_lowercase().contains("not examined")` over the whole of every study file. Step 2 keeps these semantics but does not say which fields are checked, and step 1 widens the file list to everything in studies/<dir>/. Every study must have verbatim quotes (quote_mismatch, rules.rs:339-365), and work-handling code often has an UNRESOLVED status or constant. Such a quote would fail the kept test. Changing the quote would trip quote-mismatch. A study could not satisfy both. The request's item (4) already says text quoting studied source must be exempt from word checks. Decision 5 dealt only with the lowercase-prose case. Fix: Run the placeholder check on the parsed records: every string field except `sources[].quote` of claims and rationale cards. Name the owner id in the message. Add a test that a quote containing 'UNRESOLVED' passes, alongside the existing case that claim text with 'UNRESOLVED' fails. Say in the prompt and the CHANGELOG entry that quotes are exempt from this check.

findings.summary: Matching the blanked quotes against their parsed values is fragile when the file escapes a string differently
findings.evidence: The plan parses the quotes with serde_json, then replaces the text `"quote": <literal>` wherever the literal is 'in that set'. A string's escaping in the file (for example \u escapes or \/) can differ from the parsed or re-serialized value, so the replacement can miss. The failure is safe (nothing is exempted, so the scan over-reports), but a real study could fail the scan with no clear cause. Fix: Match each `"quote"\s*:\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"` occurrence with a regex. Decode the captured literal with serde_json::from_str::<String>, and blank it when it equals a sources[].quote collected from the parsed claims. Add a test with a quote containing an escaped character.

summary: I read rules.rs (the kept firstmate tests at lines 1395-1625 and wrong_sha, cited_lines and quote_mismatch at lines 264-365), lib.rs admit(), the admit callers in run/candidate.rs and run/mod.rs, policy.rs lines 88-260, the study producer and verifier prompts, the budget lines in budgets.rs and docs/system-facts.md, the Cargo manifests and the firstmate study files. The plan's facts hold. No file sets ATHENA_PIN_*. unsafe_code is denied. tempfile is a workspace dependency. Nothing in admission scans file contents for boundary words. firstmate has only file sources and no quotes with escaped newlines. The plan's answers to the earlier rounds are sound: route-returning check_study, the synthetic tree, the degradation warning, the case-sensitive placeholder check and the budget-line update. One design fault remains. The placeholder convention now runs on every study, and as specified it still scans verbatim source quotes. That is the same false-positive class the request removes from the boundary scan: a second work-handling system whose source has an `UNRESOLVED` state would fail its own kept test. The producer could only fix that by changing the quote, which then trips quote-mismatch. This needs one change, so the verdict is revise.
